campaign: Reduce the surface of execution, evidence and development while capability and pace grow

paragraphs.text: overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is each scorecard cell against its previous measurement, not a count of landings: there is no passed state and no promotion. Rows that let a full measurement run finish rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a run that cannot finish (killed, or with cells that did not pass) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and the cycle runs them on the commit it measures; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

User-journey performance (owner, 2026-10-05). Optimize complete journeys, measured as action to usable result: submit to first visible answer, cold model selection to usable response, cancel to actual resource release, interrupted cycle to useful progress, with loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering kept apart. Start from the existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles of repeated reads, model loads, allocations and evidence reconstruction, and keep added instrumentation only when it explains a real elapsed-time gain. In the development loop one valid gate execution is shared by every compatible plan step and obligation, and validation and reuse are scoped by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated and embedded data, models, recipes, environment, subprocess effects); an unknown dependency keeps the broader coverage. A gain is judged against total maintenance cost (production code, tests, fixtures, instrumentation, gate work and upkeep): remove repeated processing through existing owners, and decline small gains that need disproportionate machinery. Prove with behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, never a new performance ratchet, selector or framework.

Pace (owner, 2026-10-09). Steps that change one mechanism land together. A measurement already taken retires the step that would take it. Work that only waits is filed early, so its wait runs while the rows between are built. A full measurement run (go run ./cmd/loop -improve) continues only at the commit it began at and is started outside a session, so no time limit ends it. Rows that move no measured result land while it runs; rows that change a served result or a timing follow it, stand side by side, and land before the next run, never between its runs.

The repository keeps Go, CUDA and HTML/JS, and extends an existing owner before it adds one. Each row begins with a measurement and fixes its acceptance before its code is written; a measurement already taken is reused when it is enough. A row deletes the implementation it replaces in the same landing; a reader that records already in the store need stays until those records are migrated. A pilot that is not accepted is taken out of the served path, and its measurements and the reason it was refused are kept.

The production growth refusal stays. A row with no count adds no net production code, which is the default: a migration deletes at least what it adds. A row that adds a mechanism before it deletes one carries a count, set in a change to the plan alone before its code, from the figure the gate's preflight gives its built change, and read from the commit the change builds on; a count set before the row is built is an estimate and says so. An item's count is for all its landings together: each landing's growth is charged to it and what is left is what the next may add. Test code, fixtures, record schemas and CUDA source are reported with each landing and not refused; a test is retired only when its replacement catches the same seeded failure.

The gate judges the candidate tree by hermetic and small-device checks; real-model quality and speed are measured by the cycle. A stored result is reused only under an unchanged identity of the code, model, recipe, data, settings and request it depends on. A request for a fresh measurement always runs, and a dependency that cannot be named keeps the wider scope. Resident resources, compiled execution and a request have separate identities, built by one mechanism into separate keys for sessions, outputs and scores. Eligibility is kept apart from selection, observations from scores, and the records that choose a candidate from the records that confirm it.

An experiment is frozen before it trains: a protocol missing a numerical gain or resource criterion is not dispatched, and a pilot does not change the acceptance of the objective it is compared with. Completing an experiment and adopting its model are separate: a complete negative or inconclusive record closes the experiment and activates nothing.

items.title: Keep the checkout, ./tmp, ./docs and the data root free of finished leftovers, by rule and by command

budget.reason: What the row may still add. Set on 2026-10-12, with plan -setcount, to the 1,772 nodes its step own-cleanup-experiments was counted at once built, by the count of syntax nodes the automated checks take, each file against the trunk's commit beb6a2137: cmd/train/main.go 232, cmd/train/pilot.go 450, internal/fsatomic/remove_unix.go 38 and remove_windows.go 89, internal/processlock/doc.go 8, and under internal/trainingworkflow change_corpus.go 4, checkpoint_steps.go 752, instruction_pilot_run.go 3, text_heldout.go 21, trained_model.go 144 and workflow.go 31; the eleven files measure 16,688 before and 18,460 after. The step's preparation estimated about 950; it was 1,255 as first built, and 517 more came from two protections the lead asked for after review: a directory in which the store registers any model is kept, and a checkpoint an earlier record kept stays kept. The step grows because a run now removes its own checkpoints where a person did. The earlier steps used the 4,228, 888 and 1,641 the row carried before. Each later step is counted the same way before it is committed.

steps.title: Have an experiment record its intermediate checkpoints as throw-away and the pilot remove its own once its record file is written
steps.rationale:
Added by the lead on 2026-10-12 from the preparation of step own-cleanup, which found that the step cannot be one commit: a run that removes its own checkpoints changes internal/trainingworkflow and cmd/train and reaches the device runs, while the command that deletes finished leftovers changes only cmd/loop and internal/guard and reaches none. This step is the first part and step own-cleanup, after it, is the second.

An experiment's run records every checkpoint it writes as a model the store registers, with a location for each file: the instruction pilot left 12, about 80 GB, that the store still names, and the capability census counts each. A checkpoint that is an intermediate product of a larger run is recorded as that, a throw-away: its document and lineage go to the store, which a held-out verdict and the corpus read, and no model and no file location does. The pilot then writes its record to a file under its output folder, syncs it, and only then removes the checkpoints it wrote, unless a reason to keep them is given, which the record states, or the reward arm is adopted. The corpus removes nothing: the proposal and the confirmation read its weights by folder, so its weights go by the deleting command once its record is committed.

Closure: internal/fsatomic gains the one tree remover a run and the deleting command both call (rename aside, then remove, so a tree is whole or gone); internal/processlock names the lock a run holds in its output folder; internal/trainingworkflow records a throw-away checkpoint and removes a run's own checkpoints, leaving any the store registers; cmd/train holds the output lock for a pilot, a corpus, a proposal and a confirmation, takes -keep-checkpoints with a reason, and writes the pilot's record file before it removes anything. Model prototypes are not touched: nothing here reads whether a model is active.

Serves: train: an experiment leaves its record and not its weights, and the census no longer grows by a pilot's checkpoints.
Disappears: the registration of an experiment's intermediate checkpoints as models; the hand redirect that was the only record of a pilot's result.
Evidence: the three tests; the next pilot's record file and receipt lines.
Batch: device, cuda and webui, through internal/fsatomic and internal/processlock; cmd/train is a command a full measurement run counts as moved.

steps.title: Have each command that makes leftovers remove its own once its record is kept
steps.rationale:
Owner rule, 2026-10-12: leftovers are always deleted by their maker once the run's record is kept, except what a committed record still reads. Today nothing does it. The reward pilot (trainingworkflow.RunInstructionPilot) left 14 checkpoints, 75 GB, and 12 of them were entered in the accepted model census at close-out (0de17a0f5). The change corpus (CollectChangeCorpus and the proposer's arms) left 24 fine-tunes and trial outputs, about 158 GB, beside a 2.5 GB experiment store that three committed records under docs/verification cite. Helper copies and temporary build folders are cleared by hand.

One door for deletion. go run ./cmd/loop -leftovers gains a delete mode: it removes only entries its table marks delete and whose finished state it has itself established, prints a receipt of each (path, bytes, the rule), and is the one command the guard admits to remove them. It never removes a backup, an entry of unknown state, or another session's unfinished work.

Experiments. A run writes its checkpoints as scratch of that run and does not register them as model candidates (RecordCheckpoint), so a throw-away checkpoint never enters the census. When the run's record is written it removes them through the door, unless a flag keeps them and says why. What a committed record reads, an experiment store, stays, and the record names it. Measure first which consumers read a registered checkpoint of an experiment today (the pilot's resume reads published checkpoints) and keep that working from the run's own directory.

Helper copies. The commit queue removes a helper copy once its commit is on the trunk and it holds nothing uncommitted, and clears its registration; a copy with uncommitted work is left and reported.

One-time, by the lead: accept the census again without the 12 pilot checkpoints, then delete the two experiments' weights through the door, keeping the change corpus's store. About 233 GB.

Split by the lead on 2026-10-12, from this step's preparation, into four commits in this order: own-cleanup-experiments before this step (a run records a throw-away checkpoint and the pilot removes its own, which reaches the device runs); this step, now the deleting command alone (go run ./cmd/loop -leftovers -delete <place>, which lists, gives a token and removes only the finished entries it listed; helper copies cleared at a commit; the guard's refusals), which reaches no longer test run; own-cleanup-withdrawal; and own-cleanup-census. This step's check is unchanged: its first test is met by the step before, and its other two fail until the deleting command exists. Decisions taken with the split: a committed record keeps an experiment's output only through its store: field; the corpus command removes nothing and its weights go by the deleting command; a helper copy in which no commit has run reads unknown and is never cleared; the experiments folder joins the guard's protected paths; the owner's data (the two experiments' weights, local branches) is listed first and removed only by a hand command outside a worker's environment.

Serves: train, and change.
Disappears: about 233 GB of experiment weights and the hand step that removes them; throw-away checkpoints in the accepted census; hand clearing of helper copies.
Evidence: free space and the census before and after; the receipt.
Batch: host for the tests. The one-time deletion changes store registrations: run cmd/validate TestAcceptedCapabilityCensus against the real store by hand after it.

On adoption (lead, 2026-10-12, at the owner's instruction to merge the review session's amendment as the lead sees fit): a model prototype is not a leftover. The owner's rule of 2026-10-12 keeps a prototype that no active model uses; this row removes what a run left behind, never code and never a registered model that is not a run's throw-away checkpoint. The first use of the delete mode on the real machine follows its own listing: the list of what will go, with bytes, is shown in the session's report before the two experiments' weights are removed, and the 12 pilot checkpoints leave the accepted census by the same published review that admitted them at 0de17a0f5.

steps.title: Withdraw the store's locations of a run's checkpoints, and only those, by a command that lists first
steps.rationale:
Added by the lead on 2026-10-12 from the preparation of step own-cleanup. The 12 checkpoints the instruction pilot wrote before step own-cleanup-experiments are registered in the installed store with a location for each file, so the listing reads their folder as held and the deleting command will not take it, and deleting the files by hand would leave the store naming files that are gone.

One command withdraws the store's locations of a run's checkpoints, and only those: for each folder under the directory named that holds a checkpoint document, the locations under that folder of the checkpoint, of what its lineage names, and of each model produced by it with that model's components. Every other location under the directory is listed as kept and not touched. It refuses the experiments folder itself, a directory outside it, a directory no committed record names, a worker's environment, and any withdrawal that would leave a component of a model with an active alias without a location. It lists first and writes only when given back the token of what it listed. The identities stay in the store without a location; a model prototype is never withdrawn by this, since only a run's own checkpoint folders are read.

Closure: cmd/loop gains the withdrawal beside the deleting command, with its receipt lines. The lead then runs it once on the pilot's run folder, after a sealed backup of the store.

Serves: train: an experiment's weights can be removed without the store naming files that are gone.
Disappears: the hold the store's registrations keep on the pilot's 80 GB.
Evidence: the test; the receipt of the one real withdrawal.
Batch: host; cmd/loop reaches no longer test run.

steps.title: Accept the store's census without the pilot's withdrawn checkpoints, then show the owner the experiments' weights to remove
steps.rationale:
Added by the lead on 2026-10-12 from the preparation of step own-cleanup. The accepted capability census (cmd/validate/testdata/accepted_census.json) binds the census of the installed store, which counts every model artifact the store holds a location for. Once the pilot's 12 checkpoints are withdrawn the store's census differs from the bound one, and TestAcceptedCapabilityCensus fails against the real store until the new census is accepted.

The lead publishes the census from a clean checkout (go run ./cmd/validate -publish-census), compares it with the bound one, files the review finding that names both, closes it with its disposition, and binds the three identities in the test data. The check reads the real store only when OVERGO_STORE_ACCEPTANCE=1 is set, as the lead sets it for this commit, and skips without it; so set, it fails between the withdrawal and this commit and passes after; the experiments' weights are deleted only after it passes, and it is run once more after the deletion, which must not move it.

Closure: test data only. The owner's data, the two experiments' weights, is then shown as the deleting command's listing and removed by the owner's word.

Serves: measure: the census a full measurement run checks is the store's.
Disappears: the 12 pilot checkpoints from the accepted census.
Evidence: the two census identities and the finding's disposition.
Batch: host; test data of cmd/validate.

steps.title: Refuse close-out while finished leftovers remain, and refuse a commit's checks below a free-space floor
steps.rationale:
Hygiene runs at three points, none a timer. The first is the end of the command that made the leftovers (step own-cleanup). This step adds the other two.

Close-out. The campaign's close-out check runs the leftovers listing and fails while any entry the table marks delete is finished, naming each. The close-out of 2026-10-12 passed with 236 GB of experiment outputs, 1,313 ./tmp entries and a stale doctrine in place.

The start of a commit's checks. They read the volume's free space once and refuse to start below a floor, with the number, and the commit's measured line reports free space. On 2026-10-11 free space went from 352 to 236 GB within two hours while 22 helper copies built; the build cache once filled the drive. The floor is a named constant derived from what the largest commit check and the full measurement run have been measured to write, with that reason beside it, not a round number.

The build cache at its source. Each helper copy builds the tree cold because a build is keyed by its directory. Measure whether building helper copies with -trimpath shares the cache, and whether that setting moves any execution identity (it is a build setting, and identities count build settings); adopt it only if stored evaluation answers stay reusable, and say what was measured either way. Clearing the cache stays the owner's approval.

Serves: change.
Disappears: the risk of a full drive during a commit or a run; close-outs that leave leftovers behind.
Evidence: a fixture below the floor refused with its number; close-out refused with one finished entry and passed with none; cache size per helper copy before and after.
Batch: host; internal/landing reaches no lane.

On adoption (lead, 2026-10-12, at the owner's instruction to merge the review session's amendment as the lead sees fit): the cache measurement is also the reopening event of the register's deferred finding ba3e2aae (a commit made from a new checkout directory reruns every package, because go's test cache holds nothing for a new directory): if helper copies come to share the cache, that finding is closed with the measurement.

decisions.question: Download the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it? The 12B FP8 twins score 0.5-1.2 nats per token worse than E4B on the guard corpus while overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers reference, so the third-party quant is the suspect.
options: Download it
Keep only the FP8 twins and record the gap
decisions.recommendation: Download it
decisions.answer: Download it

decisions.question: The capability census changed from 209 recorded identities to 220 live ones. Record a disposition that accepts the live census as the new denominator?
options: Review the 11 new identities, then accept
Accept the live census as it stands
decisions.recommendation: Review the 11 new identities, then accept
decisions.answer: Review the 11 new identities, then accept

decisions.question: Four test groups need references only the Python originals produce: the Fractale leadership tests, Krea, Pocket TTS and the Qwen3.5 projector fixture. What happens to them?
options: Delete those a running test covers, keep the rest waiting
Allow one Python run to produce the references
Keep all waiting
decisions.recommendation: Delete those a running test covers, keep the rest waiting
decisions.answer: Allow one Python run to produce the references

decisions.question: When validate-currency is otherwise ready, should the Qwen3.5-9B hybrid training proof (22m05 a cycle, the same cmd/train route and code as the blocking 4B proof) move to the background, so promotion stops waiting on every training proof? Background saves about 22 min a cycle; the 4B proof still guards the route.
options: background
blocking
decisions.recommendation: background
decisions.answer: background

decisions.question: The scorecard's serving cells (first-output, throughput, load-time, peak-device-memory) aggregate every attempt a recipe ever made: medians over all time, total tokens over total decode time, the highest peak ever. A landed improvement shows only as old samples are outnumbered and a peak never falls. Since delete-selection each cycle measures every serving cell once at the measured commit. Should those cells read the newest successful measured attempt instead, accepting one sample's timing noise in each cycle's moved list?
options: newest measured attempt
all-time aggregates
median of the newest few attempts
decisions.recommendation: newest measured attempt
decisions.answer: newest measured attempt

decisions.question: Held-out quality is unscored for forecast, image-embedding, image-gen, seq2seq, tabular and vqa because each needs a held-out set the store lacks. Answering authorizes exactly these downloads into the datasets root, each to be verified by hash once fetched: ETTh1 (github.com/zhouhaoyi/ETDataset, 2.6 MB, forecast); BFCL v3 simple (gorilla-llm/Berkeley-Function-Calling-Leaderboard, 0.3 MB, seq2seq); BeyondArena credit-g (TabArena/BeyondArena, 0.2 MB, tabular); TIFA v1.0 (github.com/Yushi-Hu/tifa, 10 MB, image-gen); A-OKVQA validation (HuggingFaceM4/A-OKVQA, 60 MB, vqa); Imagenette 160 px (fast.ai imagenette2-160, 100 MB, image-embedding). About 173 MB in all. The other five unscored rows (generation, projection, speech, training, video-gen) use sets already on disk and are not blocked.
options: Download all six (about 173 MB)
Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)
Download none and score only what is on disk
decisions.recommendation: Download all six (about 173 MB)
decisions.answer: Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)

decisions.question: The remaining models under adaptive_new/models (Wan, the Gemma configs and others) are read by tests through variables that point outside the repository, which cost environment-dependent skips. May they be copied into overgo_data/models, one model at a time, each copy verified (hash, servable identity, baseline lookup, bounded inference) before its locator switches, with the originals left in place and adaptive_new never written to?
options: Copy one at a time, verified, originals kept
Leave adaptive_new as the models' home
decisions.recommendation: Copy one at a time, verified, originals kept
decisions.answer: Copy one at a time, verified, originals kept

decisions.question: Held-out quality is unscored for generation (Fractale-350M-base) because the held-out text the proposal names, the WikiText-2 test split (Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-2-raw-v1, 0.7 MB), is not on disk: only wikitext2_train.txt is, which a model may have trained on. Answering authorizes exactly this one download into the datasets root.
options: Download the WikiText-2 test split (about 0.7 MB)
Score generation on a held-out membership of the on-disk training articles instead
Download nothing and leave generation unscored
decisions.recommendation: Download the WikiText-2 test split (about 0.7 MB)
decisions.answer: Download the WikiText-2 test split (about 0.7 MB)

decisions.question: gemma-4-12B-it-fp8 (the non-native file) is slower, heavier and slower to load than the native file at equal held-out quality (31.1 tok/s, 31.1 s load, 22.5 GiB against 41.5 tok/s, 22.6 s, 14.7 GiB; 0.4919 against 0.4926; the native file now decodes at 45 tok/s and loads in 7.5 s). Does it still serve anything that justifies the device time of its eight cycle cells and any optimization?
options: Keep it registered and measured, spend no optimization time on it
Retire it from the cycle and keep the file
Delete the file
decisions.recommendation: Keep it registered and measured, spend no optimization time on it
decisions.answer: Keep it registered and measured, spend no optimization time on it

decisions.question: Editing a pinned media runtime path (go.mod, kernels, internal/cuda, tensor, devicemath and the rest of docs/image_video_merged.json's runtime paths) needs a reviewed delta: a device receipt, a delta entry, and the registry's identity pinned in a test, built by hand twice on 2026-10-04 and again for every kernel row ahead (e4b-decode-graph, decode-small-kernels). It exists so media evidence acquired at the pinned runtime stays valid across an output-neutral edit. Since the cycle re-acquires every media cell at the commit it promotes, and its models lane runs the media acceptance tests against the frozen references, the evidence that gate protects is re-proved every cycle: it is the same per-cell currency check validate-currency deleted. Retire the registry, its pin and the gate-time check (about 600 lines of test code, the registry JSON and the landing's pinned-path rule), or keep it and build a one-command tool for it (row media-delta-command)?
options: Retire the pin, the registry and the gate-time check; the cycle's media acceptance holds the contract
Keep the pin and build the one-command delta tool (media-delta-command)
decisions.recommendation: Retire the pin, the registry and the gate-time check; the cycle's media acceptance holds the contract
decisions.answer: Retire the pin, the registry and the gate-time check; the cycle's media acceptance holds the contract

decisions.question: Speech, image-gen and video-gen quality cannot be scored by the model alone: pocket-tts outputs audio, the image generators pictures, Wan2.1 and Un-0 clips. Each proposal scores the output by a second local model: a speech recognizer for round-trip word error rate, a vision-language model for TIFA questions and for matching a clip to its caption. evaluate has no suite in which a generator's output is judged by another model, and a record must name both the generator's recipe, which the scorecard reads, and the judge's identity, which the score depends on. One judged-generation suite kind (the projection session already shows a video to Qwen3.8-27B) would serve all three rows and their eight models, with a new session for each judge modality.
options: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
Score speech by its recognizer round trip only, and leave image-gen and video-gen unscored
Leave all three unscored
decisions.recommendation: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
decisions.answer: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen

decisions.question: Held-out quality of training is scored for a recipe only by a train -objective session, which publishes a held-out verdict. Qwen2.5-0.5B trains through that route and now has its verdict (a token-prediction objective over a held-out third of the WikiText-2 articles). The other six training recipes belong to routes that prove the route rather than score text: Qwen3.5-4B and 9B hybrid-stack (a bounded observed full-stack run whose evidence is that loss descends), Wan2.1 and LiveEdit dit, Hy-Embodied mot. None of those routes holds out data or scores a model, and a token-prediction objective does not fit a diffusion or a mixture-of-transformers model. Scoring them means giving each route a held-out objective of its own (days of work each, and a 20-step proof run's held-out value says little). Which do you want?
options: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
Give each proof route a held-out objective and score its recipe
Leave the proof-route recipes unscored
decisions.recommendation: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
decisions.answer: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route

decisions.question: adaptive_new/models holds about 430 GB in 20 model directories (Krea-2-Turbo 116 GB, SenseNova-U1 66, bonzai 40, Wan2.1 33, LiveEdit 32, gemma-4-E4B 30, gemma-4-12B-fp8 29, Hy-Embodied 24, Qwen3.5-4B 18, Unlimited-OCR 13, pocket-tts 9, Qwen3.5-9B 9, then eight under 5 GB), and C: has 536 GB free at 86% full. The answer to adaptive-new-model-copies kept every original, so copying all of them leaves about 100 GB free. Which models should move into overgo_data/models now?
options: Copy the models under 10 GB now, and decide the large ones separately
Copy every model, originals kept (leaves about 100 GB free)
Copy the models under 10 GB now and leave the large ones where they are, their test variables kept
Copy the large ones too, then delete the originals after each verified copy
decisions.recommendation: Copy the models under 10 GB now, and decide the large ones separately
decisions.answer: Copy the models under 10 GB now, and decide the large ones separately

decisions.question: The ten large models under adaptive_new/models are about 204 GB of working files (their directories hold as much again in git LFS caches), adaptive_new/checkpoints is a further 211 GB and is overgo's configured checkpoints root, and C: has about 495 GB free. Copying all of it while the originals stay does not fit. How should the large models and the checkpoints root leave adaptive_new?
options: Leave them where they are for now, found through local-models.json, and take the hard-coded paths out of the tests
Move them: rename the large model directories and the checkpoints root into overgo_data (same volume, no disk cost, no copy time); this changes adaptive_new, so it needs the owner's word
Copy the large models' working files (about 204 GB, originals kept, leaves about 290 GB free) and leave the checkpoints root in adaptive_new
decisions.recommendation: Leave them where they are for now, found through local-models.json, and take the hard-coded paths out of the tests
decisions.answer: Leave them where they are for now, found through local-models.json, and take the hard-coded paths out of the tests

decisions.question: The owner told master on 2026-10-07 to take over the VAE lane and plan it as master sees fit. The lane's own plan is 32 steps, none started, behind about 3000 lines of contracts with no caller. What shape does the work take on master?
options: Five measured rows on master, each lane file ported with its first caller, optional branches unplanned until a proposer is kept
Merge the lane's contracts whole and follow its 32-step plan in order
Keep only the installed-autoencoder capability and its held-out measure, and retire the rest of the campaign
decisions.recommendation: Five measured rows on master, each lane file ported with its first caller, optional branches unplanned until a proposer is kept
decisions.answer: Five measured rows on master, each lane file ported with its first caller, optional branches unplanned until a proposer is kept

decisions.question: Load NVIDIA's cuDNN library for the video codec's convolutions, the way cuBLAS is loaded? It is a new native dependency and a further install for a user, and its results are not guaranteed bit for bit across versions and devices.
options: Load it for the codec comparison
Keep only overgo's own kernels
decisions.recommendation: Load it for the codec comparison
decisions.answer: Load it for the codec comparison

decisions.question: May a served value differ from the double-precision host reference, within a tolerance written down before the change, when it is held to the model's own code at the precision that code uses?
options: Allow it under a tolerance declared first
Keep value-for-value agreement with the host reference
decisions.recommendation: Allow it under a tolerance declared first
decisions.answer: Allow it under a tolerance declared first

decisions.question: May more than one session commit, each from its own worktree, through one queue?
options: Yes, through one queue
Keep one committing session
decisions.recommendation: Yes, through one queue
decisions.answer: Yes, through one queue

decisions.question: The GUI lane's worktree was removed on 2026-10-09 and the lane left what it recommends and did not land in the main checkout, as docs/gui_update_plan.json: a deadline on every browser wait, a top-p control in Settings, the output size shown before an export, the Train tab's samples shown while a run goes, rsLoRA and LoRA+ offered for an adapter run, a few demo datasets, documents turned into a conversation dataset, the resident model kept only when it fits beside a training run, and whether a chat turn needs the request number a workflow run carries, with its notes for starting a lane again. The file is not committed: nothing reads it, the repository keeps no document without a reader, and it is ignored in that checkout so it stays as the lane left it. None of the nine is a row of this plan and none has a session. Who takes them?
options: Rank them into this plan after the rows that move a measured result
Open a GUI lane for them again
Leave them recorded and unranked
decisions.recommendation: Rank them into this plan after the rows that move a measured result
decisions.answer: Rank them into this plan after the rows that move a measured result

decisions.question: identity-carry was filed to carry an evaluation only while the code it depends on is unchanged and to delete the sampled replay. Measured 2026-10-09: 46 of the 87 newest results stand on a replay-carried result, 30 of them carried 19 or 20 times; scoring those 46 in full took 13 hours 55 minutes; the code an evaluation depends on changed on 112 of the last 300 commits and cycles lie hundreds of commits apart, so with the replay deleted every cycle scores them all again, about 14 hours more a cycle. The replay's sample is the same 32 cases every time, so a change that misses them is never seen. What should carrying do?
options: Carry under an unchanged identity, else by a replay whose sample changes each time
Carry only under an unchanged identity and score the rest in full every cycle
Leave carrying as it is
decisions.recommendation: Carry under an unchanged identity, else by a replay whose sample changes each time
decisions.answer: Carry only under an unchanged identity and score the rest in full every cycle

decisions.question: evaluation-chain's last step, acceptance, adds a memory ceiling and a speed target to a held-out pool's acceptance and has a confirmation refuse a candidate with no resource comparison against the base within them. Every candidate the proposer makes today is other weights of the base's shape, so it has the base's memory and speed, and no row in the plan makes another kind of candidate; a served recipe's memory and speed are already read by the scorecard and by the routing decision. When should the step be built?
options: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed
Now, ahead of such a candidate
Not at all: leave memory and speed to the scorecard and the routing decision
decisions.recommendation: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed
decisions.answer: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed

decisions.question: The video codec can now convolve a clip of about ten frames or more through NVIDIA's cuDNN. Measured beside another job on the device: a decode about a third faster, an encode about a fifth, the decoder holding 6.0 GiB where it held 9.6, and every value within one of 255 levels of what overgo's own kernels give. It does so only on a machine where cuDNN is on the search path or in the bin directory CUDA_PATH names. This machine's only copy is inside a Python environment, so it still serves by the kernels and the automated checks skip the library's tests. Installing it is yours to do: cuDNN 9 for CUDA 12, about 800 MB, from NVIDIA under NVIDIA's license. The frozen video clips are the kernels' bytes, and I would accept them again under the library afterwards. Install it here?
options: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it
Keep this machine on the kernels; the library stays for machines that have it
Take the library's path back out
decisions.recommendation: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it
decisions.answer: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it

decisions.question: Should the text objective eventually change from mean per-document likelihood improvement to the frequency of document wins? Many small wins can coexist with a materially worse mean. The instruction-following pilot does not require this change.
options: Keep the current likelihood objective; decide any replacement only after calibration in likelihood units
Authorize a separate proposal for document-win frequency with an explicit magnitude safeguard and its own calibration
decisions.recommendation: Keep the current likelihood objective; decide any replacement only after calibration in likelihood units
decisions.answer: Keep the current likelihood objective; decide any replacement only after calibration in likelihood units
